articles.title: Road Closures Planned for Milaad Procession in Rochdale from 24 August 2026
articles.excerpt: Road closures will be in effect in Rochdale for the Milaad Procession starting on 24 August 2026, as announced by local authorities.
articles.content_html:
A series of road closures will take place in Rochdale from 24 August 2026 to accommodate the Milaad Procession. Local authorities have confirmed the closures to ensure the safety of participants and spectators during the event.

Details regarding the specific roads affected by the closures have yet to be released. Residents and motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and seek alternative routes during this period.

The Milaad Procession is an annual event celebrating the birth of the Prophet Muhammad, attracting participants from various communities.

Further information about the event and the exact road closures will be provided closer to the date.

articles.title: Roadworks on Princess Street to Begin on 7 September 2026
articles.excerpt: Queen Street in Rochdale will be closed for roadworks from 7 September to 17 September 2026, affecting traffic flow in the area.
articles.content_html:
A section of Queen Street will be temporarily closed for roadworks from 12 midnight on Monday, 7 September 2026, until 11.59pm on Thursday, 17 September 2026.

The closure will affect the stretch of Queen Street between the junctions with Whitehall Street and Duke Street. During this period, no waiting will be allowed in this area.

Motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly, as the roadworks may impact traffic flow.

For more information, residents can view a map of roadworks across Greater Manchester on the Rochdale Borough Council website.

articles.title: Two men injured in Heywood crash on Moss Hall Road
articles.excerpt: Two men were taken to hospital with serious injuries following a crash involving two cars on Moss Hall Road in Heywood.
articles.content_html:
A crash involving two cars occurred on Moss Hall Road in Heywood at around 7.45am on Tuesday, July 28. Two men, aged 35 and 44, were taken to hospital with serious injuries, according to a spokesperson for Greater Manchester Police.

Emergency services, including police and paramedics, attended the scene. An air ambulance also landed nearby. Residents reported that a section of the road was closed for several hours following the incident.

Officers from Greater Manchester Police's Serious Collision Investigation Unit are investigating the crash. They have requested that anyone who witnessed the incident or has relevant footage, such as CCTV or dashcam recordings, come forward with information.

Anyone with information can contact police on 0161 856 4741 or via the Live Chat service, quoting log 616 of 28/07/26. Alternatively, information can be reported anonymously to Crimestoppers at 0800 555 111.

articles.title: Roadworks on Birtle Road in Heywood to Begin on 24 August 2026
articles.excerpt: Birtle Road in Heywood will undergo roadworks from 24 to 28 August 2026, resulting in a temporary closure affecting traffic flow.
articles.content_html:
Birtle Road in Heywood will be temporarily closed for roadworks from Monday, 24 August 2026, to Friday, 28 August 2026. The closure will take place daily from 10am to 4pm.

The affected section of Birtle Road will be closed starting at the junction with Gristlehurst Lane and extending 95 metres southward. Due to the nature of the closure, there will be no alternative route for vehicles.

Motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly, as the closure may impact traffic flow during the specified hours.

For further details, residents can view a map of roadworks across Greater Manchester on the Rochdale Borough Council website.

articles.title: Hopwood Triangle Traffic Trial to Continue Pending Township Vote
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council has confirmed that the Hopwood Triangle traffic calming trial will remain in place until a formal township vote is conducted to decide its future.
articles.content_html:
A traffic calming trial around the Hopwood Triangle in Heywood will continue pending a formal vote by the Heywood Township, Rochdale Council has announced. The trial, which introduced several changes to local roads, has faced significant criticism from motorists and residents since its implementation.

The measures include the closure of Middleton Road at its junction with Manchester Road near St John's Church, aimed at preventing drivers from using the route as a shortcut. Additionally, Magdala Street has been made one way towards Manchester Road, and new parking restrictions for heavy goods vehicles, along with a 20mph speed limit, have been introduced on surrounding residential roads.

North Heywood councillor Bev Place expressed disappointment that the trial would not end as soon as she had hoped. She stated that highways officers informed her that a township meeting must first vote to formally conclude the trial. Councillor Place is working to arrange an extraordinary meeting, as the next scheduled meeting is not until 22nd September.

In response to the ongoing concerns, a Rochdale Council spokesperson indicated that there is no set date for the removal of the traffic restrictions and that they are in discussions with contractors regarding the situation. Residents are encouraged to submit their views to the council's highways team via email to ensure their opinions are formally considered.
